subject: Incident notification & handback: KMS access and evidence scope
messages:
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: daphne.li@orchardhealth.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Incident notification & handback: KMS access and evidence scope

Hi Daphne —

Thanks again for jumping on the call earlier. To summarize and make sure we have clear next steps in writing: Orchard has asked for a narrow evidence export and, in parallel, clarification on our KMS handling and whether any key material needs to be shared with your appointed forensics vendor. Per Section 7.2 of your DPA and our standard notification clause, I want to outline what Redwood can commit to and what we need from you to proceed.

Proposed items Redwood can action immediately:
- Provide a time-bounded export of telemetry and request/response metadata scoped to affected customer IDs (export window: T-72 to T+1).
- Generate cryptographic audit logs for the same window (hashes only; we will not share raw HSM-protected keys).
- Engage our approved forensics partner (SecProve) to run a controlled snapshot if you provide a POA and signed evidence access form.

Questions / asks for Orchard:
1) Confirm the exact account IDs and the minimal PII set you need for your investigation (we will not export broader user lists without explicit approval).
2) Clarify whether you require Redwood to escrow any key material or whether a signed HSM proof-of-possession will suffice.
3) Provide contact and scope for your forensics vendor (name, contact email, signed processing agreement if not already on file).

Attachments: incident_scope_matrix.xlsx (draft mapping of logs -> retention -> export format); kms_key_snapshot.txt (high-level record of key IDs, not secret material).

Timing: we can prepare a scoped export within 48 hours of receiving: (a) account ID confirmation, (b) signed access form, and (c) confirmation of vendor processing terms. If the event meets the DPA notification threshold for personal data exposure, please confirm whether you expect the 72-hour notification window to start at detection or at mutual acknowledgement — we'll align on timestamps.

I'll loop in Kimberly and Karthik to coordinate technical exports and legal checklist.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: daphne.li@orchardhealth.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@orchardhealth.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident notification & handback: KMS access and evidence scope

Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Affected accounts: orchard-prod (customer IDs: ORCH-1183, ORCH-1184). We only need the request traces and token metadata (no full text of patient notes).
- For the KMS: we do not want raw keys. We need either a) an HSM-signed assertion that keys were not exported and the key IDs used for the affected workloads, or b) a sealed export to our forensics vendor under a mutually agreed transfer protocol.
- Our vendor: SecProve (forensics@secprove.com). They require a Processing Addendum; I have attached a redline we typically use (I'll forward separately to your legal).

On timelines: Orchard expects an initial handover plan within 24 hours (high-level: who does what, timelines), and a scoped export within 72 hours where technically feasible. If Redwood believes any of these timelines are not feasible, flag asap so we can escalate.

We have also requested temporary escalation rights in the DPA for cross-border transfer of hashed telemetry — will confirm after legal review.

Thanks,
Daphne Li
Head of Security Operations
Orchard Health

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, daphne.li@orchardhealth.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident notification & handback: KMS access and evidence scope

Daphne / team —

Legal ops checklist (quickly):
- DPA trigger: Confirmed risk threshold met per clause 4.1 (unauthorized access to request metadata). This means we must "use commercially reasonable efforts" to provide cooperative support.
- Transfer constraints: if any exported telemetry contains EU-origin data we will need a documented lawful basis/justification for transfer; please advise jurisdictional breakdown if relevant.
- KMS handling: Redwood will not share raw master key material. Options we can offer: 
  1) HSM-signed attestations + key IDs + derived-key verification artifacts (preferred), or
  2) Controlled sealed export to a named vendor with dual-signature pickup (requires DOJ-style chain-of-custody steps and signed evidence release from Orchard).

Operational ask for Karthik: can you stage the following?
- Prepare a hashed telemetry export (CSV) and a separate request-metadata JSON (redacted) covering ORCH-1183/1184 for T-72 -> T+1 window.
- Produce KMS audit hashes and an HSM attestation PDF.
- Stand up a SecProve intake workspace (S3 bucket w/ restricted credentials) that we can use for sealed export if required.

Karthik, please estimate time to ready artifacts and whether you need any additional approvals (HSM ops, infra).

Kimberly Park
Director, Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: daphne.li@orchardhealth.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, forensics@secprove.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 13:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident notification & handback: KMS access and evidence scope

Thanks all — short update and commitments: 

1) Plan:
- Within 6 hours: Redwood will send a high-level handover plan (who owns each step, expected SLA for each artifact).
- Within 48 hours: hashed telemetry export + redacted request-metadata for ORCH-1183/1184.
- Within 72 hours: HSM-signed attestation and KMS audit-hashes. If Orchard confirms sealed export is required instead of an attestation, we will need the signed evidence release and a brief POA for SecProve; that will add an estimated 24 hours to the export window.

2) Security & transfer notes:
- Redwood will not provide raw key material from our HSMs. Any transfer of derived artifacts will use asymmetric wrapping and dual-control pickup.
- If cross-border transfer of hashed telemetry is necessary, we will follow standard SCC/transfer mechanisms and document the lawful basis.

3) Attachments: incident_scope_matrix.xlsx (updated with confirmed account IDs) and kms_key_snapshot.txt (key IDs + HSM slot info; non-secret).

Action items: 
- Daphne: confirm acceptance of HSM attestation vs sealed export (reply all).
- SecProve: confirm receipt and whether your intake requires additional metadata (forensics@secprove.com).
- Karthik: begin staging exports and confirm ETA by EOD.

We will treat this as high priority — Kimberly and Grace will lead legal/ops coordination.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
